name: TV OS (Debian + Kodi)
provision:
apt-get update
DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends kodi xserver-xorg xinit dbus-x11 pulseaudio
useradd -m -G video,audio,input,tty kodi || true
printf '[Unit]
Description=Kodi
After=systemd-user-sessions.service network-online.target

[Service]
User=kodi
Group=video
PAMName=login
TTYPath=/dev/tty7
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/bin/xinit /usr/bin/kodi-standalone -- :0 -nolisten tcp vt7
Restart=always

[Install]
WantedBy=graphical.target
' > /etc/systemd/system/kodi.service
systemctl set-default graphical.target
systemctl enable kodi.service
notes: The plan's own worked example of a recipe, and the answer for architectures LibreELEC publishes no image for: a base cloud image plus a script that turns it into a television. It costs nothing to host because there is nothing to host - the base is Debian's own download and this is a few lines of text. Not the same thing as LibreELEC, and it does not pretend to be; it is a machine that watches things, for one script rather than a port. Building it boots the base with a cloud-init seed, runs the script, and the guest powers itself off when it is done - which is how the mod knows a build finished, because nothing else about a script is visible from outside a guest. Then the result is frozen as this entry's template and every television after it clones it in seconds. Reach it with /give @s virtualcomputers:custom_os[virtualcomputers:image_id="tv_kodi"].
